text:
### Observed differences

- Participation is unchanged: A15, A17, A18, A19, A20 and A21 co-occur in every trace in both windows (200 of 200 traces on each side), and A26 and A27 also appear in essentially all traces in both windows, so the difference lies in execution order, not in whether the activities run [REL001, REL004, REL006, LAG005, LAG024].
- In the earlier window there was no fixed order among these activities: A15 preceded A19 in only about 26 in 100 cases, A17 preceded A19 in about 50 in 100, A18 preceded A19 in about 12 in 100, A15 preceded A21 in about 50 in 100 and A18 preceded A20 in about 47 in 100 — most pairs appeared in both orders across cases [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007].
- In the later window a single order prevails: A15 before A19 in 199 of 200 cases, A18 before A19 in 199 of 200, A18 before A21 in 199 of 200, and A17 before A19, A15 before A21, A17 before A21 and A15 before A20 in 200 of 200 [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL008].
- Spacing collapsed from variable to fixed: the A17→A18 gap was spread over 2–5 positions earlier (2 steps in about 32 in 100 of observed cases) but is exactly 2 in 199 of 200 later traces; A15→A18 went from 1 step in about 62 in 100 (remainder spread over 2–4) to 1 step in 199 of 200; A15→A20 went from a 1–4 spread to exactly 4 steps in 199 of 200 [LAG001, LAG003, LAG007].
- The later distances fit one back-to-back sequence, A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27: A26→A17, A17→A15, A15→A18, A19→A21, A21→A20 and A20→A27 are each 1 step in essentially every later trace, and longer pairs (A15→A19 at 2, A18→A21 at 2, A15→A20 at 4, A26→A21 at 5) match the summed distances [LAG001, LAG002, LAG006, LAG012, LAG017, LAG020, LAG022, LAG029].
- Reverse ordered pairs that were common earlier almost disappear: A19 then A15 within five steps occurred in about 149 of 200 earlier traces but only 1 later trace (A15 then A19: 51 earlier vs 199 later), and A20 then A18 in about 106 earlier versus 1 later; each of these later profiles rests on a single observation [LAG002, LAG014, LAG019].
- Relative positions shifted only slightly, in the direction the reordering implies: A15, A17 and A18 now occur slightly earlier within traces (mean relative position about 0.64→0.59, 0.59→0.56 and 0.68→0.62) and A19, A20 and A21 slightly later (about 0.59→0.65, 0.68→0.71 and 0.64→0.68) [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports one specific hypothesis: a change in the ordering constraints over the activity group A15, A17, A18, A19, A20 and A21, executed between A26 and A27 — from mixed, case-varying orders in the earlier window to a single fixed sequence in the later window, consistent with A26 → A17 → A15 → A18 → A19 → A21 → A20 → A27 run consecutively at fixed spacing. This is a change in ordering constraints, not a path replacement or an exchange of positions: every activity occurs in virtually every trace in both windows, and what changed is that both orders per pair collapsed into one [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008].

The change is shown directly and consistently: all eight measured activity pairs flipped from both-orders-present to essentially one order, each backed by 200 traces per window [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]; all 24 pair-distance distributions collapsed from spreads to single fixed values that fit the same chain [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG007, LAG012, LAG017, LAG020, LAG024, LAG025, LAG029]; screening flagged 43 control-flow items against about 0.33 expected without change, a volume chance cannot account for [screening]. The POS, REL and LAG items describe the same underlying reordering, so they corroborate rather than independently confirm it; all 43 flagged items concern these eight activities' relative order or spacing, and no other behavioural difference appears at the configured thresholds [screening].

Limitations: POS and LAG use event positions within the case, not clock time, so the evidence concerns order and spacing, not timing; a few reverse-direction distance profiles (A19→A15, A20→A18) rest on a single later trace and are weak alone, though the hypothesis does not rely on them [LAG014, LAG019]. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the earlier mixture was a small set of distinct fixed variants rather than per-case flexible ordering — each pair had a definite order within a trace (no interleaving or repetition) but different orders across cases — so the change may be a consolidation of variants into one sequence; the observable ordering behaviour changed as described under either reading [REL001, REL004, REL006].
